headline: Colom announces town hall in reddest county of Mississippi
author: Ford McCracken

paragraphs.text: Sen.-elect Scott Colom (D-Miss.) will hold a town hall next Tuesday in the county where he received the lowest share of the vote in the midterms, he announced earlier this week, aligning with the Democrat’s pledges to be “a senator for all Mississippi.”

“Itawamba County is where I received my lowest percentage of the vote on Election Day. But I promised to be a senator for all Mississippi and I meant it,” Colom wrote in Facebook post Thursday. “No matter where you live or how you voted, your voice matters and I’ll always show up for you.”

Itawamba County is in northeast Mississippi, just east of the city of Tupelo. President Trump carried the county by 80 points in 2024 and received the highest share of the vote in county history for a Republican presidential candidate. Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R), whom Colom unseated in this year’s Senate race, won Itawamba by nearly 66 points.
The town hall invitation describes the event as “an opportunity to hear directly from Senator-elect Colom, ask questions, and engage in meaningful dialogue.”

Colom defeated Hyde-Smith in a massive upset that took days after the election to call. He is the first Black senator Mississippians have elected by popular vote and the third to ever represent the Magnolia State — the last being Sen. Blanche K. Bruce, who served during the post-Civil War Reconstruction era. Although the state of Mississippi is one third Black, according to census data.
The senator-elect made reaching out to Republicans a focal point of his Senate campaign, something he had to do in order to be elected in deep-red Mississippi.

One viral video he posted to social media showed him speaking with voters in line for Trump’s Mississippi rally just days before the election. Colom said in an interview Friday speaking with Trump voters showed him they had a lot in common and were dissatisfied with similar issues.

“I want to represent those people. So, it was my job to go listen to them, and I found out we had a lot in common,” Colom told MS NOW’s Ari Melber. “They were saying the same stuff I was hearing across the state: high gas, high groceries, get out of the war in Iran.”
Even Trump chimed in to Colom’s appearance at his rally, saying in an interview with sports commentator Stephen A. Smith he gave the Democrat “a lot of credit” for campaigning in his line.
